spacr.division_analysis.frame_effects:
Hedges' g of dividing against control units at every frame before division.

Both tables are baseline-normalised aligned values (each unit relative to
its own first frames, as in the trajectories of :func:`analyse_divisions`).
At each ``rel_t`` from ``-window`` to 0 the dividing units' own values
(``role == 'self'``) are compared with the control units' own values with
:func:`effect_size`, measure by measure.

:param dividing: baseline-normalised values of the dividing units, with
    ``role``, ``rel_t`` and one column per measure.
:param control: the same for the matched control units.
:param window: frames before division in the alignment window.
:param columns: the measures compared; absent ones are skipped.
:param n_boot: bootstrap resamples per frame and measure.
:param rng: seed or generator for the resampling.
:returns: one row per measure and ``rel_t`` with the :func:`effect_size`
    columns (``g``, ``var_g``, ``ci_low``, ``ci_high``, ``mean_diff``,
    ``n_treated``, ``n_control``).
spacr.division_analysis.onset_times:
When each measure's pre-division change starts.

For one measure, the per-frame effects (:func:`frame_effects`) up to the
division (``rel_t <= 0``) are read from the division backwards. The
direction is the sign of ``g`` at the last frame before division. A frame
is significant when its interval excludes 0 in that direction. When the
last frame is not significant there is no onset (NaN, with the direction
still given); otherwise the onset is the earliest ``rel_t`` of the
unbroken significant run that ends at the division.

:param effects: per-frame effects with ``measure``, ``rel_t``, ``g`` and
    the interval columns.
:param settings: run settings; ``timelapse_division_onset_ci`` names the
    interval columns as ``'low/high'`` (default ``'ci_low/ci_high'``).
:param measures: the measures reported, in order; None takes those in
    ``effects`` in the order they first appear. A measure without rows
    gets NaN for both.
:returns: one row per measure with ``measure``, ``onset_rel_t`` (frames,
    0 or negative, NaN without an onset) and ``direction`` (+1 rises, -1
    falls before division).
:raises ValueError: for an interval setting that is not ``'low/high'`` or
    names columns ``effects`` does not have.
spacr.division_prediction.division_predi:
A precision-recall curve thinned to about ``points`` points, as the reference.

:param y: the labels (0/1).
:param score: the predicted scores; non-finite scores are left out.
:param points: the most points kept, evenly spaced along the curve.
:returns: ``recall`` and ``precision`` columns; empty without both classes.
spacr.division_prediction.lineage_trees:
The root of every track's lineage tree.

:param lineage: lineage table with ``label`` and ``parent``.
:returns: ``{label: root label}``, following parents up to a track
    without a known parent.
spacr.division_prediction.prediction_fea:
The :func:`division_prediction_features` keyword arguments of a run.

``timelapse_division_prediction_frames='auto'`` is max(2, round(0.15 x
median cycle)) and ``timelapse_division_prediction_lag='auto'`` is
min(alignment window, 5), both from the division analysis summary.

:param settings: the run settings.
:param summary: the field's division analysis summary (``window``,
    ``median_cycle_frames``), needed for the automatic values.
:returns: ``frames``, ``history``, ``feature_set``, ``lag``,
    ``born_flag``, ``events`` and ``negative_rule``.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown feature set, events or negative rule.
spacr.division_prediction.prediction_run:
The :func:`predict_divisions` keyword arguments of a run, beyond model and folds.

:param settings: the run settings.
:returns: ``one_per_track``, ``sample_seed``, ``max_rows``,
    ``row_seed``, ``min_positive_tracks``, ``min_positive_rows``,
    ``arms``, ``group``, ``learner`` (None for today's learner) and
    ``seed``.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown unit, arm or group.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.ashman_d:
Ashman's D between the control mode N(0, 1) and N(mu1, s1^2).

:param mu1: the responder mode's mean.
:param s1: its standard deviation.
:returns: ``sqrt(2) |mu1| / sqrt(1 + s1^2)`` (Ashman et al. 1994); above
    2 the two modes are clearly separated.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.cell_cycl:
Each cell's cell-cycle phase: G1, S/G2 or M.

:param cells: one row per cell.
:param dna: the integrated nuclear DNA (DAPI) intensity column,
    flat-field corrected.
:param control: True for a non-targeting cell.
:param mitotic: the boolean mitotic-call column (the DNA rule of
    :func:`mitotic_calls` or a trained classifier).
:param group: the column whose groups (wells) find their own G1 peak.
:param split_log2: interphase cells this far above the G1 peak, in log2
    units, are S/G2 (``ops_profile_g1_sg2_split_log2``; 0.30 is about
    1.23 times G1 DNA, the dip of the non-targeting histogram on Funk
    plate A).
:param mode_cells: the cells the G1 peak is found on; by default the
    non-targeting interphase cells.
:returns: ``phase`` (``'G1'``, ``'SG2'`` or ``'M'``) and
    ``dna_log2_rel`` (log2 DNA minus the group's G1 peak), on the index
    of ``cells``.

The G1 peak is the mode of the smoothed histogram of log2 DNA content
(:func:`g1_mode`), found per well on the non-targeting interphase cells,
so a knockout that piles cells up in S/G2 does not move it.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.contrasti:
Weight gene profiles by how far each direction rises above guide noise.

:param genes: one row per gene with ``gene``, ``n_cells`` and the
    ``features``; non-targeting rows (names starting with
    ``control_prefix`` or ``NTpseudo``) are kept as rows but not fitted.
:param guides: one row per guide with ``guide``, ``gene``, ``n_cells``
    and the same ``features``. The non-targeting guides give the noise.
:param features: the profile columns.
:param control_prefix: the control gene prefix.
:param min_cells: genes with this many cells or fewer are left out
    first; None keeps every gene.
:param variance: the share of variance the embedding keeps.
:param seed: the PCA seed.
:param drop_zero: leave out the directions whose weight is 0. The
    cosine of two rows is the same either way.
:returns: ``(gene_rows, guide_rows, info)``: ``gene, n_cells, w_0 ...``
    and ``guide, gene, n_cells, w_0 ...`` in the weighted space, and
    ``lambda``, ``weights``, ``directions_kept``, ``kbar`` and
    ``nt_guides``.
:raises ValueError: when fewer than two directions have lambda above 1.

The gene rows are embedded (standardised, PCA 99 %) and the guide rows
put in the same space. The noise covariance is the Ledoit-Wolf
covariance (Ledoit & Wolf 2004) of the centred non-targeting guide rows,
divided by ``kbar``, the mean number of guides per targeting gene, since
a gene profile pools that many guides. The generalised eigenproblem
``Sigma_genes v = lambda Sigma_noise v`` gives directions ordered by
signal over noise; each is weighted by ``max((lambda - 1) / lambda,
0)``, a Wiener weight. This is a contrastive eigenproblem in the spirit
of contrastive PCA (Abid et al. 2018).

IT REFUSES A DEGENERATE SPACE. On profiles already shrunk toward the
controls (:func:`shrink_gene_profiles`) no direction rises above the
noise, every weight is 0 and every row the zero vector; a retrieval
score then ranks ties first and reports AP = 1. Do not stack the two.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.disk_offs:
The pixel offsets of a disk sampled on a grid.

:param radius: the disk radius in pixels (``ops_neighbour_radius_px``).
:param grid: the sampling step in pixels (``ops_neighbour_grid_px``).
:returns: ``(dy, dx)``; radius 50 on a 2-pixel grid gives 1,961 offsets.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.distribut:
Each gene's energy distance to the controls and its sliced
Wasserstein embedding.

:param cells: as :func:`responder_profiles`.
:param features: the profile columns.
:param control: True for a non-targeting cell.
:param options: passed to :func:`responder_profiles`, whose random
    stream also draws the responder folds, so the distances are the
    same as in its summary.
:returns: ``(distances, embedding)``: ``gene`` and
    ``energy_distance_vs_NT``, and one sliced Wasserstein row per gene.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.embedding:
Gene profiles from frozen single-cell embeddings.

:param embedding: one row per exported cell (a NumPy array or memory
    map, any float dtype); only the rows of ``rows`` are read, a chunk
    at a time, so a large export stays on disk.
:param cells: one row per profiled cell, in the order of ``rows``, with
    ``guide``, ``gene`` (non-targeting cells under pseudo-gene names,
    :func:`nt_row_names`; ``nontargeting_drop`` cells are left out of
    the profiles) and ``well``.
:param control: True for a non-targeting cell.
:param rows: the embedding row of each cell; by default ``0..n-1``.
:param guide: the guide column.
:param gene: the gene column.
:param well: the well column (the batch).
:param norm: ``'tvn'`` (per-well centre-scale, PCA 99 % fitted on a
    ``sample``-cell sample, then TVN on the control cells with CORAL by
    well, :func:`spacr.ops_tvn.tvn_on_controls`) or ``'robustz'``
    (per-well robust z against the control cells, then PCA 99 %).
:param sample: cells the PCA is fitted on.
:param seed: the sample and PCA seed.
:param chunk: embedding rows read at a time.
:param whiten_epsilon: the TVN whitening epsilon; 0 is Brieflow's TVN.
:returns: ``(genes, info)``: ``gene, n_guides, n_cells, emb_0 ...``
    (a guide is the median of its cells, a gene the median of its
    guides) and ``components`` and ``cells``.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown ``norm``.

The cells are the ones the measurements were profiled on, so the
embedding and measurement profiles of :func:`fusion_profiles` describe
the same cells.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.escaper_c:
Are escaper genes guide-driven, cell-cycle-coupled or genotype errors?

:param genes: the ``genes`` table of :func:`penetrance_tests`.
:param cells: its ``cells`` table with ``phase`` and, per cell, the
    genotype-error probability ``e``, ``n_exact``, ``runner_margin``,
    ``source`` and ``n_reads`` of the genotype confidence model.
:param controls: non-escaper genes analysed the same way, the control.
:param seed: the seed of the control draw.
:returns: ``(table, summary)``: one row per escaper and control gene
    with the responder and non-responder genotype-error rates (and a
    one-sided Mann-Whitney P), phase composition (chi-square P),
    responder shares in well-supported and single-read cells, Ashman's
    D (:func:`ashman_d`) and ``escaper_class``.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.escaper_s:
Does a gene's response split its cells into responders and escapers?

:param z: the gene cells' z scores against held-out control cells.
:param dbic: the BIC margin the mixture must win by
    (``ops_escaper_dbic``).
:param min_separation: the responder mode's least distance from the
    controls, in control standard deviations (``ops_escaper_min_sep``).
:returns: ``(statistics, posterior)``: ``dBIC``, ``mix_p``,
    ``mix_mu1``, ``mix_s1``, ``shift_delta``, ``shift_kappa`` and
    ``escaper_raw``, and each cell's responder probability.

Two models are compared: a unimodal shift ``N(delta, kappa^2)`` (two
parameters) and the controls plus a responder mode, ``(1 - p) N(0, 1) +
p N(mu1, s1^2)`` (three). A gene is an escaper candidate when the
mixture wins by ``dbic``, ``0.1 <= p <= 0.9`` and ``mu1`` is at least
``min_separation``.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.field_fol:
The cross-fitting fold of every field, fixed by its name.

:param wells: the well of every cell.
:param sites: the field (site) of every cell.
:param folds: the number of folds.
:returns: the fold of every cell: the first eight hex digits of the md5
    of ``"<well>|<site>"`` modulo ``folds``, so a field is in the same
    fold for every gene and every run.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.fitness_b:
Quantile bins of log cells per guide; the lowest bin is fitness genes.

:param genes: gene names; non-targeting rows get -1.
:param cells_per_guide: each gene's cells per guide.
:param bins: the number of bins.
:param control_prefix: the control gene prefix.
:returns: the bin of every gene, 0 the most depleted.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.fusion_pr:
Gene profiles of several blocks joined with equal weight.

:param blocks: name -> gene table (``gene``, ``n_cells`` and profile
    columns starting ``PC_``, ``emb_`` or ``f_``), in join order; the
    first block's cell counts are kept (``ops_fusion_blocks``).
:param variance: the share of variance each block keeps.
:param seed: the PCA seed.
:returns: ``gene, n_cells, f_<block>0 ...`` for the genes every block
    has.

Each block is standardised across genes, PCA-whitened to ``variance``
and divided by the square root of its dimension count, so a block's
squared norm averages one whatever its width, and a 768-dimension
embedding cannot outvote a 100-dimension measurement profile.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.g1_mode:
The G1 peak of a log2 DNA-content distribution.

:param log_dna: log2 integrated nuclear DNA intensity of interphase
    cells.
:param bins: histogram bins between the 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles.
:param smooth: the Gaussian smoothing of the histogram, in bins.
:returns: the centre of the highest bin of the smoothed histogram.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.generic_c:
Per-gene covariates of fitness and cell-cycle arrest.

:param genes: one row per gene with ``gene``, ``n_guides`` and
    ``n_cells`` (:func:`aggregate_genes`).
:param cells: one row per cell with ``gene`` and ``phase``
    (:func:`cell_cycle_phases`).
:param control: True for a non-targeting cell.
:param gene: the gene column of ``cells``.
:param phase: the phase column of ``cells``.
:returns: ``gene, n_guides, n_cells, frac_G1, frac_SG2, frac_M,
    cells_per_guide, shift_G1, shift_SG2, shift_M``: each phase's share
    of the gene's cells, and that share minus the non-targeting cells'
    share.

Cells per guide falls when a knockout kills or slows cells, so it is a
fitness readout of the screen itself; the phase shifts measure arrest.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.guide_eff:
Gene profiles that weight each guide by how well it knocks down.

:param genes: the gene rows :func:`contrastive_weighting` returns
    (``gene``, ``n_cells``, ``w_*``); with the cell level of
    :func:`aggregate_genes` they are the all-cell gene medians.
:param guides: its guide rows (``guide``, ``gene``, ``n_cells``,
    ``w_*``).
:param columns: the profile columns; by default the ``w_*`` columns.
:param iters: the most alternations per gene (``ops_guide_efficacy_iters``).
:param emax: the cap on an efficacy before rescaling
    (``ops_guide_efficacy_emax``).
:returns: ``(rows, efficacy)``: one row per gene, ``gene, n_cells`` and
    the columns of ``Z/|Z| + M/|M|``, whose cosine is the similarity;
    and the efficacy of every guide, indexed by guide.
:raises ValueError: when the weighted space has fewer than two
    directions, as :func:`contrastive_weighting` refuses.

THE GUIDE MODEL IS JACKS' RANK-1 MODEL (Allen et al. 2019, Genome Res,
doi:10.1101/gr.238923.118), with the profile features in the role of
JACKS' screens: each guide row is ``x_g = e_g m + noise``, the noise
variance proportional to ``1 / n_cells(g)``. Starting from ``e = 1``,
``m = sum w e x / sum w e^2`` (``w`` the cell counts) and ``e =
clip(<x, m> / <m, m>, 0, emax)`` alternate, ``e`` rescaled so its
maximum is 1, for at most ``iters`` rounds or until ``e`` changes by
less than 1e-6. The efficacy-weighted profile ``M`` is then blended
with the all-cell gene profile ``Z`` as unit vectors. A gene row
without guide rows keeps ``Z``. The method uses no reference labels.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.guide_lev:
Gene-gene similarity from guides, with a P value for every pair.

:param guides: one row per guide with ``gene`` and the ``features``;
    non-targeting guides carry pseudo-gene names (:func:`nt_row_names`).
:param features: the profile columns.
:param genes: the targeting genes whose pairs are tested (the active
    genes in the published analysis); by default every targeting gene.
:param control_prefix: the control gene prefix.
:param null_size: random guide-set pairs per pair of set sizes
    (``ops_guide_null_size``); P values resolve to ``1 / (N + 1)``.
:param control_null_size: non-targeting guide-set pairs in the reported
    control null.
:param seed: the seed of the one random stream.
:param alpha: the false discovery rate of ``pairs_q05``.
:returns: ``pairs`` (``gene_a, gene_b, s, p, q`` for every tested pair),
    ``calibration_p`` (the pseudo-gene x gene P values, the control),
    ``similarity`` and ``names`` (the gene x gene matrix, tested genes
    then pseudo-genes) and ``summary``.

The guides are embedded as the benchmark embeds them (standardised, PCA
99 %, fitted on the guides) and scaled to unit length; ``s(A, B)`` is
the mean of the ``k_A x k_B`` guide-guide cosines. The null of a pair
is ``null_size`` similarities between two random guide sets of the same
sizes, each guide from a distinct random targeting gene, so a P value
asks whether two genes agree more than random guides do. Benjamini-
Hochberg gives ``q`` across all pairs. The pseudo-genes, paired with
every tested gene, should give uniform P values; the share under 0.05 is
the calibration control. Non-targeting guide sets give a second null,
reported for comparison. Without reference sets this does not annotate
pairs with CORUM or STRING; :mod:`spacr.ops_clusters` scores those.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.guide_mea:
Each gene as the mean of its guides' unit vectors.

:param guide_rows: one row per guide, in an embedded space.
:param guide_genes: the gene of every guide.
:param normalise: scale each mean to length 1, so the dot product of
    two genes is the cosine of their means.
:returns: ``(genes, vectors, guides_per_gene)``, genes sorted.

Without ``normalise`` the dot product of two genes is exactly the mean
of their ``k_A x k_B`` guide-guide cosines. That rewards a single-guide
row (length 1) over a gene whose guides disagree (length below 1), and
on Funk plate A single-barcode control rows then filled 58 % of the top
ten neighbours; normalising removes that.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.mask_neig:
Every cell whose mask reaches within ``radius`` of a cell's nucleus.

:param cell_mask: one field's cell label image (0 is background).
:param labels: the receivers' labels in that image.
:param centroids: their nucleus centroids, ``(row, col)`` per receiver.
:param radius: the neighbourhood radius in pixels.
:param grid: the disk is sampled on this grid, so a neighbour that
    touches the disk only in a sliver narrower than ``grid`` can be
    missed.
:returns: ``(pairs, receivers)``: ``r_label, n_label, n_px`` (neighbour
    mask pixels on the sampled disk) per pair, the receiver itself left
    out; and per receiver ``label, cy, cx, edge_dist,
    disk_occupied_frac, n_nbr``. Neighbours are any segmented cell,
    genotyped or not.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.neighbour:
Does a knockout change its unperturbed neighbours?

:param wells: per well ``(cells, receivers, pairs)``: the analysed cells
    (``site, label, sgRNA, gene`` and the ``features``), the receiver
    table and the neighbour pairs of :func:`mask_neighbours` (with a
    ``site`` column).
:param features: the profile columns.
:param active: genes with a phenotype of their own; their cells are
    never receivers.
:param receivers: ``'inactive'`` (own gene non-targeting or inactive)
    or ``'nt'`` (own gene non-targeting only)
    (``ops_neighbour_receivers``).
:param null_reps: replicates of each null (``ops_neighbour_null_reps``).
:param edge_px: receivers nearer the field edge are left out.
:param field_centre: the field centre in pixels, for radial position.
:param seed: the base seed of the nulls.
:returns: ``tests`` (``gene, n_exposed, T, kind, p_clone, q_clone,
    p_shuffle, q_shuffle``), ``nulls``, ``d``, ``V`` and ``names``.

A receiver is exposed to gene X when a genotyped neighbour carries X; a
neighbour with the receiver's own guide never counts, so clone sisters
are not exposures, and the reference is exposure to a control
neighbour. Receiver features are its TVN components minus its own
gene's mean in the well, residualised within field on local density
and radial position (Frisch-Waugh-Lovell). The statistic is ``T =
sum_d d^2 / (v_X + v_ref)``, ``d`` the exposed-minus-reference mean and
``v`` its field-clustered variance. Nulls: genotypes shuffled within
each field, and a clone-preserving shuffle that moves whole same-guide
clusters; the control pseudo-genes are exposures too. ``p`` is
empirical against the pooled null genes of the same exposure-count
quintile, ``q`` Benjamini-Hochberg across genes.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.nt_row_na:
The gene name each cell (or guide) gets when controls become rows.

:param guides: the guide of every row.
:param genes: the gene of every row; a name starting with
    ``control_prefix`` (any case) marks a non-targeting guide.
:param rows: ``'pseudo'`` groups the non-targeting guides at random into
    pseudo-genes of ``group_size``, named ``NTpseudo_00``,
    ``NTpseudo_01``, ...; ``'barcode'`` makes every non-targeting guide
    its own row, named ``<control_prefix>_<guide>``.
:param control_prefix: the control gene prefix.
:param nt_guides: the non-targeting guides the pseudo-genes are drawn
    from; by default those among ``guides``. Pass the full set when only
    part of the cells is named, so every part gets the same groups.
:param group_size: guides per pseudo-gene.
:param seed: the permutation seed.
:param drop_incomplete: name the guides of a last, smaller pseudo-gene
    ``nontargeting_drop`` so they can be left out.
:param pseudo_prefix: the pseudo-gene name before its two-digit number.
:returns: the gene names; targeting rows keep their gene.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown ``rows``.

The pseudo-genes are drawn as in the improved Funk plate A analysis:
the sorted unique non-targeting guides are permuted with
``numpy.random.default_rng(seed)`` and guide ``i`` goes to pseudo-gene
``rank_i // group_size``, where ``rank_i`` is its position in the
permutation. A pseudo-gene is processed exactly as a gene, so it is the
null a gene's statistic is compared against. One row per barcode is
Brieflow's layout (Di Bernardo et al., Nat Commun 2026).
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.penetranc:
Per-gene penetrance and escapers, with their controls.

:param cells: one row per cell with ``guide``, ``gene``, ``well``,
    ``site`` and the ``features`` (TVN components).
:param features: the profile columns.
:param genes: the genes to test, in order (the active genes).
:param control: True for a non-targeting cell.
:param guide: the guide column.
:param gene: the gene column.
:param well: the well column.
:param site: the field column.
:param folds: cross-fitting folds (``ops_penetrance_folds``).
:param control_pool: control cells drawn once, in proportion to each
    well, as every gene's reference (``ops_penetrance_nt_pool``).
:param lam: the Storey lambda (``ops_penetrance_lambda``).
:param reps: field-bootstrap draws for the interval.
:param simulations: unimodal simulations an escaper call must beat.
:param min_cells: genes with fewer cells are not tested.
:param shuffled: genes rerun with shuffled labels, the second control.
:param dbic: the escaper BIC margin (``ops_escaper_dbic``).
:param min_separation: the escaper mode separation
    (``ops_escaper_min_sep``).
:param seed: the seed of the control pool, the bootstrap and the
    shuffled-gene draw.
:returns: ``genes``, ``controls``, ``guides`` and ``cells`` tables with
    the columns of the published analysis.

EVERY CELL IS SCORED BY A MODEL THAT NEVER SAW ITS FIELD. Fields go to
folds by name (:func:`field_folds`). For each fold an L2 logistic
regression (balanced classes) is trained on the gene's and the
controls' cells of the other folds, and the held-out gene cells are
placed on the held-out control cells: ``u`` is their control
percentile, uniform without an effect, and ``z`` their control z score.
The penetrance is Storey's estimator on ``u`` (:func:`storey_penetrance`)
with a 95 % interval from resampling whole fields; escapers are tested
on ``z`` (:func:`escaper_statistics`), and a call stands only if none
of ``simulations`` unimodal simulations of the fitted shift makes it.
Guides are compared by the share of their cells above half the
responder mode (chi-square). CONTROLS: the non-targeting pseudo-genes
(:func:`nt_row_names`) scored against the pool without their own
cells, which should show no penetrance; and ``shuffled`` genes whose
gene and control labels are permuted, whose penetrance should fall to
the real cells' share times the gene's penetrance.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.phase_col:
The profile columns ``ops_profile_cell_cycle`` keeps.

:param table: a :func:`phase_profiles` table.
:param profile: ``'concat'`` for every phase, or one phase name.
:returns: the ``<phase>_<feature>`` columns of the chosen phases.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown profile.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.phase_pro:
Guide and gene profiles resolved by cell-cycle phase.

:param cells: one row per cell with ``phase``, ``group``, ``guide``,
    ``gene`` and the ``features`` (TVN components in the published
    analysis).
:param features: the profile columns.
:param control: True for a non-targeting cell.
:param phase: the phase column (:func:`cell_cycle_phases`).
:param group: each group (well) is centred on its own controls.
:param guide: the guide column.
:param gene: the gene column.
:param phases: the phases profiled, in column order.
:param drop_genes: gene names left out of both tables after the
    centring (the guides :func:`nt_row_names` could not group).
:returns: ``(guides, genes)``. The guide table has ``guide, gene`` and
    per phase ``<phase>_n_cells`` and ``<phase>_<feature>``; a guide
    with no cell in a phase has NaN there. The gene table has ``gene``
    and the ``<phase>_<feature>`` columns: the median of its guides.

Within each well and phase, every cell is first centred on the median of
the well's non-targeting cells of the same phase. A profile then shows
what the knockout changes within a phase, not that it moves cells
between phases (the phase fractions say that). The concatenated profile
``[G1 | S/G2 | M]`` keeps the three apart. A gene's cells therefore count
in the phase they are in.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.phase_tes:
Which genes change cells in one cell-cycle phase only?

:param cells: one row per cell with ``guide``, ``gene`` (non-targeting
    cells under pseudo-gene names, :func:`nt_row_names`), ``well``,
    ``phase`` and the ``features``.
:param features: the profile columns.
:param control: True for a non-targeting cell.
:param guide: the guide column.
:param gene: the gene column.
:param well: the well column.
:param phase: the phase column (:func:`cell_cycle_phases`).
:param null: ``'targeting'`` calibrates on random sets of four
    targeting guides of four genes, ``'nt'`` on random sets of four
    control guides (``ops_phase_null``).
:param null_sets: random sets the null is fitted on.
:param fresh_sets: with the targeting null, fresh random sets scored as
    genes, the held-out check.
:param seed: the seed of every profile's null.
:returns: ``tests`` (one row per gene and profile), ``calls`` (one row
    per gene, with ``specific_<phase>``, ``specific_<phase>_interaction``
    and ``composition_only``) and ``summary``.

Profiles are ``pooled`` (every cell, centred on its well's controls) and
each phase (that phase's cells, centred on the well's controls of the
same phase); a guide is the median of its cells, with at least three.
A gene's statistic is ``T = sum_d M_d^2 / V_d`` over the dimensions,
``M`` the mean of its guides and ``V_d = (1/K^2) sum_j (a_d + b_d /
n_j)``, the noise fitted on the control guides of the first half of the
pseudo-genes; the second half is held out. ``T`` is referred to a scaled
chi-square matched to the null sets' mean and variance. The targeting
null is the main one: every targeting guide cuts DNA, control guides do
not, so against controls almost every gene differs pooled. The
interaction profiles test a phase against the gene's other cells.
A gene is phase-specific when its phase ``q < 0.1`` (Benjamini-Hochberg)
and its pooled ``q >= 0.1``.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.remove_ge:
Regress fitness and arrest out of gene profiles.

:param values: one row per gene, the profile columns.
:param genes: the gene of every row.
:param covariates: :func:`generic_covariates`, indexed by gene or with a
    ``gene`` column; every gene of ``genes`` must be in it.
:param axes: what to remove (``ops_profile_generic_axes``):
    ``log_cells_per_guide`` and the ``shift_<phase>`` covariates are
    regressed out; ``essential_axis`` also projects out the fitness
    genes' main direction when it tracks fitness.
:param min_rho: the essential axis is removed only when the genes'
    scores on it correlate with log cells per guide by more than this
    in absolute Spearman rho (``ops_profile_essential_axis_min_rho``).
:param control_prefix: non-targeting rows are corrected but not fitted.
:param guide_values: optional guide rows of the same space, corrected
    with the same fit.
:param guide_genes: the gene of every guide row.
:returns: ``(residuals, report, axis, guide_residuals)``. The report
    holds ``var_removed_by_covariates``, ``covariates``,
    ``essential_genes``,
    ``essential_axis_rho_with_log_cells_per_guide``,
    ``essential_axis_removed`` and, when removed,
    ``var_removed_by_essential_axis``.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown axis.

Each profile column is fitted across the targeting genes by ordinary
least squares on the standardised covariates (intercept kept), and the
covariate part is subtracted from every row, non-targeting rows
included. The essential axis is the first right singular vector of the
uncentred profiles of the lowest decile of cells per guide
(:func:`fitness_bins`); it is projected out only when it tracks
fitness, so a profile direction that merely contains many fitness genes
stays.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.responder:
Per gene: which of its cells respond, how they differ, and how far
its cell distribution is from the controls'.

:param cells: one row per cell with ``guide``, ``gene`` and the
    ``features`` (TVN components).
:param features: the profile columns.
:param control: True for a non-targeting cell.
:param guide: the guide column.
:param gene: the gene column; non-targeting cells carry pseudo-gene
    names (:func:`nt_row_names`) so they are processed as genes.
:param use: the cells to use (interphase cells in the published
    analysis, with ``nontargeting_drop`` cells left out); all by default.
:param alpha: the share of control cells a threshold lets through
    (``ops_profile_responder_alpha``).
:param folds: cross-fitting folds.
:param max_cells: a gene with more cells is subsampled to this many.
:param control_pool: control cells drawn once as the reference.
:param min_cells: genes with fewer cells are skipped.
:param energy_cells: gene cells in the energy distance and the sliced
    Wasserstein embedding.
:param energy_controls: control cells in the energy distance.
:param directions: random projections of the sliced Wasserstein
    embedding.
:param quantiles: quantiles per projection.
:param seed: the seed of the one random stream.
:returns: ``summary`` (``gene, cells_used, flagged_frac,
    responder_fraction, energy_distance_vs_NT, responders``),
    ``genes`` (``gene`` and the responder-shift profile),
    ``guides`` (``guide, gene, responders`` and its profile) and
    ``sliced_wasserstein`` (genes x ``directions * quantiles``).

RESPONDERS ARE CALLED BY A CROSS-FITTED DISCRIMINANT. Per fold, the
direction is the gene's mean minus the controls' mean on the other
folds, and a cell is flagged when its projection exceeds the held-out
controls' ``1 - alpha`` quantile. The responder fraction is ``(flagged
- alpha) / (1 - alpha)``, floored at 0: the share of the gene's cells
with the phenotype, its penetrance. The responder profile is the mean
of the flagged gene cells minus the mean of the flagged control cells
(the plain mean difference when fewer than five of either are
flagged), so a phenotype carried by a few cells is not diluted by the
rest. A control cell of the gene's own guides is never its reference.

The energy distance (Szekely & Rizzo 2013) compares ``energy_cells``
gene cells with ``energy_controls`` control cells. The sliced
Wasserstein embedding (Bonneel et al. 2015) gives each gene the
``quantiles`` quantiles of its cells along ``directions`` fixed random
directions, so the Euclidean distance between two embeddings
approximates their sliced Wasserstein distance.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.shrink_ge:
Gene profiles shrunk toward the controls by their guides' reliability.

:param guides: one row per guide with ``gene``, ``n_cells`` and the
    ``features`` (TVN components, whose per-cell variance is about 1).
:param features: the profile columns.
:param control_prefix: genes whose name starts with it (or with
    ``NTpseudo``) are the non-targeting rows that set the noise.
:param n_cells: each guide's cell count; by default ``n_cells``.
:param prior_df: the degrees of freedom of the non-targeting noise
    estimate when it is pooled with a gene's own guide spread
    (``ops_profile_shrinkage_prior_df``).
:returns: ``(genes, factor, parameters)``: one row per gene, ``gene``
    and the shrunk ``features``; each gene's mean shrink factor; and
    ``a_between``, ``tau2`` and ``prior_df``.

Per feature ``d``, a guide's noise is the between-guide variance
``a_d`` of the non-targeting guides plus the sampling variance of a
median of ``n`` cells, ``(pi / 2) v_d / n`` with ``v_d = 1``. For each
gene that noise, averaged over its guides, is pooled with the gene's own
between-guide variance (``K - 1`` degrees of freedom against
``prior_df``), so a gene whose guides disagree is shrunk more. The
prior signal variance ``tau2_d`` comes from the moments of the
targeting genes, and the gene's mean guide profile, centred on the
non-targeting guides, is multiplied by ``tau2 / (tau2 + V / K)``. This
is empirical-Bayes variance moderation (Smyth 2004) followed by a
James-Stein-type shrinkage. Do not stack it with
:func:`contrastive_weighting`, which then has no direction left.
spacr.gene_measurement_compare.storey_pe:
The share of a gene's cells that carry its phenotype.

:param u: each gene cell's percentile among held-out control cells
    (uniform when the gene has no effect).
:param lam: the percentile below which only non-responders are assumed
    to fall (``ops_penetrance_lambda``).
:returns: ``1 - F(lam) / lam``, Storey's estimator (Storey 2002) of the
    non-null share: non-responding cells look like controls, responding
    cells sit above the controls' median.
spacr.host_pathogen.analyze_titration:
An HRMAn-style infection and replication readout across a titration.

Vacuoles and cells come from :func:`vacuole_objects` (or saved tables).
Every well gets its strain, status and dose from
``titration_plate_map``. Vacuoles under the parasite-signal floor
(:func:`infection_floor`) are dropped and cells are called infected from
the kept vacuoles. With ``replication_classifier='hist_gbm'`` the
classifier is cross-validated on ``replication_training_table``
(:func:`replication_classifier_cv`) and predicts parasites per vacuole
after the size calibration (:func:`size_calibration`, on the kept
vacuoles of infected wells). Writes titration_vacuoles.csv,
titration_per_well.csv, titration_per_condition.csv,
titration_calibration.txt and replication_classifier_cv.txt to
``<src>/results/titration/``.

:param settings: ``src`` and the :data:`TITRATION_DEFAULTS` keys.
:returns: dict with ``vacuoles``, ``wells``, ``conditions``,
    ``calibration``, ``floor`` and ``cv`` (None without a classifier).
spacr.host_pathogen.classify_replication:
Parasites per vacuole from a classifier trained on an external table.

The classifier (``replication_classifier='hist_gbm'``) is trained on the
training table's columns; each vacuole is described by the mapped spaCR
columns, areas multiplied by ``k`` and lengths by sqrt(``k``), missing
values filled with the column median.

:param vacuoles: the vacuole table.
:param training: the training table.
:param settings: the replication settings.
:param k: the size calibration factor (:func:`size_calibration`).
:returns: the predicted parasites per vacuole, one per vacuole row.
:raises ValueError: for ``replication_classifier`` other than
    ``'hist_gbm'``.
spacr.host_pathogen.infection_floor:
The parasite-signal floor below which a vacuole is not counted.

``infection_signal_floor`` is ``'none'`` (no floor), a number, or
``'uninfected_percentile'``: the ``infection_floor_percentile``
percentile of ``infection_signal_column`` over the vacuoles found in the
``infection_uninfected_wells`` (or the wells with status
``uninfected``).

:param vacuoles: the vacuole table (with ``status`` when no wells are
    named).
:param settings: the floor settings.
:returns: the floor, or None for no floor.
:raises ValueError: when the percentile has no uninfected vacuole to read.
spacr.host_pathogen.modal_area:
The modal object area on a log scale.

Areas under ``min_size`` are left out; the log areas are binned into
``bins`` equal bins and the centre of the fullest bin is returned.

:param areas: object areas in pixels.
:param min_size: smallest area counted.
:param bins: histogram bins.
:returns: the modal area in pixels.
spacr.host_pathogen.nuclear_translocatio:
The host-nucleus effector translocation readout of a plate, from settings.

Reads the merged arrays of ``translocation_merged_folder`` (or
``<src>/merged``). With ``cell_from_nucleus_expand_px`` above 0 a
five-plane array ``[c0, c1, c2, nucleus, parasite]`` gets its cell plane
from the nuclei first (:func:`nucleus_territories`) and becomes the
six-plane layout; a six-plane array already has its cell plane (Make
Masks grows the territories itself with the same setting) and is read
as it is. Cells are marked ``cell_source`` nucleus_territory when the
territories were grown here or the merged folder's plane layout says
Make Masks grew them; the territories are not cell outlines. Then
:func:`translocation_cells` per field and :func:`translocation_summary`,
written to ``<src>/translocation/`` (cells_translocation.csv, the
summary tables, reference_curve.csv when ``translocation_reference``
names a reference curve table, and the
translocation_ratio_vs_vacuoles figure of :func:`translocation_figure`).

:param settings: ``src`` and the translocation settings.
:returns: the :func:`translocation_summary` dict with ``folder`` and
    ``figure`` (the path written).
spacr.host_pathogen.nucleus_territories:
Cell masks from nuclei when there is no cell stain.

Nuclei under ``min_nucleus_size`` pixels are removed, then every nucleus
grows by up to ``expand_px`` pixels without overlapping another
(:func:`skimage.segmentation.expand_labels`, a distance-capped Voronoi
territory). The territories are not cell outlines.

:param nucleus_mask: integer nucleus mask.
:param expand_px: the largest growth in pixels.
:param min_nucleus_size: the smallest nucleus kept.
:returns: ``(territories, nuclei)`` as int32 masks; a territory has its
    nucleus's label.
spacr.host_pathogen.replication_classifi:
Cross-validate the replication classifier on its own training table.

Reports the majority-class accuracy, the area quantiles (10%, 50%, 90%)
per class, and the ``replication_cv_folds``-fold accuracy of the
classifier on the area column alone and on every training column, each
for the classes themselves and for 'more than one parasite'.

:param training: the training table (e.g. HRMAn's Training_dataset.csv).
:param settings: ``replication_training_columns``,
    ``replication_class_column``, ``replication_classes``,
    ``replication_seed`` and ``replication_cv_folds``.
:returns: dict with ``majority``, ``quantiles`` (a DataFrame),
    ``scores`` (a DataFrame of feature set, target and accuracy) and
    ``text`` (the report as written).
spacr.host_pathogen.size_calibration:
The factor that puts spaCR vacuole sizes on an external reference scale.

With ``size_calibration='modal_single'``,
k = ``size_calibration_reference_px`` / :func:`modal_area` of the
vacuole areas: the reference single-parasite area over spaCR's modal
vacuole area. Areas are multiplied by k and lengths by sqrt(k);
``'none'`` gives k = 1.

:param vacuole_areas: areas of the vacuoles of infected wells.
:param settings: ``size_calibration``, ``size_calibration_reference_px``
    and ``vacuole_min_size``.
:returns: dict with ``k``, ``reference_px`` and ``modal_px``.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown ``size_calibration``.
spacr.host_pathogen.titration_conditions:
Per-condition means and SDs of the wells that pass QC, beside reference values.

:param wells: the table from :func:`titration_wells`.
:param reference: optional reference values with ``strain``, ``dose``,
    ``metric`` (``repl`` or ``size``), ``value`` and ``err``; they become
    the ``HRMAn pct_replicating`` and ``HRMAn mean_size`` columns and
    their ``err(as stored)`` columns.
:returns: one row per strain, status and dose, values rounded to 2
    decimals, with ``wells``, ``cells`` and ``vacuoles``.
spacr.host_pathogen.titration_wells:
Per-well infection, replication and vacuole size.

Columns as the reference titration_summary: cells, infected_cells,
vacuoles, vacuoles_unhosted, mean_vacuole_area_px, parasites per
vacuole and % replicating (classifier and linked-parasite counts),
pct_infected, vacuoles_per_100_cells and ``qc_pass`` -- False for a well
with fewer than ``titration_min_well_cells`` times the median cell count
of its condition.

:param cells: per-cell table with ``well``, ``strain``, ``status``,
    ``dose``, ``cell`` and ``infected``.
:param vacuoles: per-vacuole table with ``n_parasites_clf``,
    ``n_parasites_cellpose``, ``repl_clf`` and ``repl_cellpose``.
:param settings: ``titration_min_well_cells``.
:returns: the per-well table, sorted by strain, status, dose and well.
spacr.host_pathogen.translocation_cells:
Per-host-cell nuclear effector signal and vacuole counts of one field.

``stack`` is a merged array ``[..., c]`` with the image channels and, at
planes 3, 4 and 5, the cell (territory), nucleus and parasite masks.
Parasites under ``translocation_min_pathogen_size`` pixels are dropped;
vacuoles are :func:`vacuoles_from_parasites` with ``vacuole_gap_px``;
parasites and vacuoles go to the cell holding most of their pixels.
Nucleus pixels within ``translocation_exclude_px`` of a parasite pixel
are excluded from the corrected readout; the field background is the
median effector signal outside every cell and parasite (the
``translocation_background_fallback_percentile`` of the field when fewer
than ``translocation_background_min_px`` such pixels).

:param stack: the merged array.
:param settings: :data:`TRANSLOCATION_DEFAULTS` and ``vacuole_gap_px``.
:param well: the well name written into the table.
:param field: the field number written into the table.
:returns: one row per cell with a nucleus: nucleus_area, n_parasites,
    n_vacuoles, ha_total_nucleus (raw sum over the nucleus),
    ha_mean_nucleus, ha_total_nucleus_excl, ha_mean_nucleus_excl,
    frac_nucleus_excluded, ha_mean_cyto, cyto_area, dna_mean_nucleus and
    bg_ha (``ha`` is the ``translocation_channel``, ``dna`` the control
    channel).
spacr.host_pathogen.translocation_summar:
Effector translocation against vacuoles per cell, with its controls.

Every cell gets its group from ``translocation_groups`` (by well row, or
by well from a plate map) and two readouts: raw (``ha_total_nucleus``)
and corrected (``(ha_mean_nucleus_excl - bg_ha) x nucleus_area``). Cells
with nuclei under ``translocation_min_nucleus_size`` are left out.
Curves bin cells by k = vacuoles per cell up to ``translocation_kmax``
and divide by the k = 0 cells of the same group; per-well ratios use
wells with ``translocation_min_cells_per_bin`` cells in the bin. The
controls are the k = 0 reference, the ``translocation_null_percentile``
threshold of the corrected mean in k = 0 cells (% positive nuclei per k
and per well), the within-field shuffle of k (``translocation_shuffle_n``
times, seed ``translocation_seed``, group by group, raw then corrected),
the DNA control, nucleus area and the excluded fraction.

:param cells: :func:`translocation_cells` rows of every field.
:param settings: the translocation settings.
:param reference: an optional reference curve (effector, k,
    hrman_total, hrman_ratio) for the agreement table.
:returns: dict of DataFrames ``cells``, ``counts``, ``curves``,
    ``per_well``, ``per_well_summary``, ``null_thresholds``,
    ``pct_positive``, ``pct_positive_per_well``, ``shuffle_null`` and
    ``agreement`` (empty without a reference).
spacr.host_pathogen.vacuole_objects:
Per-vacuole and per-cell tables of one field.

Vacuoles come from :func:`vacuoles_from_parasites`; each one under
``vacuole_min_size`` pixels is dropped. Its host is the cell label most
of its pixels lie on (``host_assignment='majority_overlap'``), 0 when it
lies on no cell or the cell is under ``host_min_size`` pixels. Cells
under ``host_min_size`` are dropped; a cell is infected when it hosts a
vacuole.

:param cell_mask: integer host-cell mask.
:param parasite_mask: integer parasite mask of the same shape.
:param intensity: the parasite-channel image for ``tox_mean``, or None.
:param settings: :data:`TITRATION_DEFAULTS` keys.
:param well: the well name written into both tables.
:param field: the field number written into both tables.
:returns: ``(cells, vacuoles)`` with the columns of the reference
    titration_objects script.
:raises ValueError: for another ``host_assignment``.
spacr.host_pathogen.vacuoles_from_parasi:
Group touching or nearly touching parasites into vacuoles.

The parasite foreground is closed with a 4-connected structuring element
``gap_px`` times (parasites up to about ``gap_px`` pixels apart join),
every original parasite pixel is kept, and the result is labelled.
Parasite-to-vacuole parentage is :func:`vacuole_links` (majority overlap).

:param parasite_mask: integer parasite mask, zero background.
:param gap_px: closing iterations.
:returns: ``(vacuole_mask, links)``; ``links`` is None for an empty mask.
spacr.ml.annotation_sample:
A stratified sample of ``n`` objects to annotate.

Every stratum (each combination of the ``strata`` keys) contributes up to
``ceil(n / number of strata)`` objects drawn with ``seed``; when that
falls short of ``n`` the rest is drawn from what is left, spread over
the first key with ``seed + 1``. The result is shuffled with
``seed + 2`` and cut to ``n``. A stratum key ``column:q`` bins the column
into q quantiles by rank within each value of the first key.

:param df: the objects to sample from.
:param n: how many objects to keep.
:param seed: the sampling seed.
:param strata: comma-separated stratum keys, e.g. ``'strain,
    rim_enrichment:5'``; blank samples without strata.
:returns: the sampled rows, with a ``stratum`` column.
spacr.ml.classifier_metrics:
Accuracy, balanced accuracy, macro F1, AUROC and per-class precision and recall.

:param y_true: the true labels.
:param y_pred: the predicted labels.
:param classes: every class, in the order of the ``y_score`` columns.
:param name: the model name of the row.
:param y_score: class probabilities (one column per class), or None; the
    AUROC is one-vs-rest macro for three or more classes and NaN without
    scores or with one class present.
:returns: one metrics row as a dict, with ``<class> precision``,
    ``<class> recall`` and ``<class> n`` for every class.
spacr.ml.evaluate_classifier:
Evaluate a classifier with held-out folds and controls.

The model of ``ml_model_type`` is trained on every fold of
``ml_eval_split`` (:func:`evaluation_folds`) and predicts the held-out
rows. One row per fold and one pooled row (every held-out prediction
together) are reported. The controls of ``ml_eval_controls`` are
reported the same way: ``majority`` always predicts the commonest label
of the whole set; ``shuffled`` trains on labels permuted within each
training fold, repeated ``ml_eval_shuffle_repeats`` times with seeds
``ml_eval_shuffle_seed``, ``ml_eval_shuffle_seed + 1``, ... and
averaged.

:param df: the labelled objects with a ``label`` column, the
    ``features`` and the grouping columns of the split.
:param features: the feature columns.
:param settings: ``ml_eval_split``, ``ml_eval_controls``,
    ``ml_eval_shuffle_seed``, ``ml_eval_shuffle_repeats``,
    ``ml_model_type``, ``n_estimators`` and ``ml_eval_random_folds``.
:returns: the metrics table (:func:`classifier_metrics` columns plus
    ``role`` -- model or control -- and ``fold``, ``'pooled'`` for the
    pooled rows).
:raises ValueError: for an unknown split, control or model type, or
    fewer than two classes.
spacr.ml.evaluate_classifier.add: Append the pooled row and one row per fold of one prediction set.
spacr.ml.evaluation_folds:
The train and test rows of every evaluation fold.

``'leave_one_well_out'`` holds out one well at a time (the ``well``
column, else plate, ``rowID`` and ``columnID``), in sorted order;
``'leave_one_plate_out'`` one plate (``plateID`` or ``plate``);
``'random'`` is a stratified ``n_splits``-fold split shuffled with
``seed``.

:param df: the labelled objects; its index is kept.
:param split: one of :data:`ML_EVAL_SPLITS`.
:param seed: shuffling seed of the random split.
:param n_splits: folds of the random split.
:returns: a list of ``(fold_name, train_index, test_index)``.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown split or missing grouping columns.
spacr.ml.export_annotation_sample:
Mark a stratified sample of objects for the Annotate screen.

Draws :func:`annotation_sample` from ``png_list`` of
``<src>/measurements/measurements.db`` (joined to
``ml_eval_features_table`` on ``ml_eval_join_column`` when the strata
need its columns) and writes the draw order (1..N) into the png_list
column ``annotate_sample`` with spaCR's png_list column writer, so the
Annotate screen can show just those crops. ``ml_label_column`` is
created empty when missing and never overwritten.

:param settings: ``src``, ``annotate_sample_n``, ``annotate_sample_seed``,
    ``annotate_sample_strata`` and optionally ``ml_eval_features_table``.
:returns: the sampled rows with their ``annotate_sample`` order.
spacr.ml.run_ml_evaluation:
Write the held-out evaluation of a classifier to ``results/ml_eval/``.

Without ``df`` the objects come from ``ml_eval_features_table`` joined
to the ``ml_label_column`` labels in ``png_list`` (the evaluation-only
run :func:`generate_ml_scores` makes when that table is set). Rows whose
label is missing or not in ``ml_eval_classes`` are left out.
:func:`evaluate_classifier` does the evaluation.

:param settings: run settings; ``src`` (the first source folder takes
    the results), ``ml_label_column``, ``ml_eval_classes``,
    ``ml_eval_features`` (blank: every numeric column but the label)
    and the :func:`evaluate_classifier` settings.
:param df: the objects, already joined to their labels, or None.
:param features: the feature columns, or None for ``ml_eval_features``.
:returns: dict with ``metrics`` (the table), ``path`` (``metrics.csv``),
    ``n`` and ``classes``.
:raises ValueError: when no feature column is left, or the
    :func:`evaluate_classifier` errors.
spacr.ops_decode:
Decode rules, decoy FDR and decode QC for optical pooled screens (alpha).

Purpose and scope
=================
:func:`spacr.ops_engine.run_ops` decodes every field of a well. This module
holds the parts of that decode that the BMC decode-yield study added
(items 873, 876, 877 and 878), so that a settings run reproduces the study's
final rule rather than a script over a field cache:

* the field rule "rule (a) + S2" (:func:`field_calls`): library-calibrated
  base calls, territory attribution, quality-weighted votes, the runner-up
  one-mismatch rule and the pixel fallback, matched against the library and
  a decoy library;
* the decoy FDR report of every decode (:func:`fdr_report`,
  :func:`plate_fdr_summary`);
* the per-field evidence a field's calls were made from, in the cache layout
  the study used (:func:`field_evidence`), which the decode QC reads.

Every rule here is off unless its setting turns it on, so a decode that

spacr.ops_reference:
Gene-gene reference sets for scoring optical pooled screen gene profiles.

A gene profile is judged by how well it finds the genes a curated resource
links to it. This module reads those resources by name and version, turns
each into a set of unordered gene pairs ``(a, b)`` with ``a < b``, and splits
them into the halves of a selection protocol, so that a choice made on one
half is reported on the other.

The names, and the file each one is read from inside ``reference_dir``:

* ``CORUM`` and ``KEGG``: Brieflow's group benchmarks
  (``corum_group_benchmark.tsv``, ``kegg_group_benchmark.tsv``; columns
  ``gene_name`` and ``group``); every two members of a group are a pair.
* ``STRING_brieflow``: Brieflow's STRING pair benchmark
  (``string_pair_benchmark.tsv``; ``gene_name`` and ``pair``).
* ``STRING>=0.7`` and ``STRING>=0.4``: STRING v12 links with a combined
  score of at least 700 or 400 (``string_v12_ge400.parquet``, made by
  :func:`prepare_current_references`).
* ``BioGRID``: BioGRID physical human pairs, latest release
  (``biogrid_physical.parquet``).
* the references known when Funk et al. 2022 was published and the evidence
  added later, made by :func:`prepare_time_split_references`:
  ``STRING11.5>=0.7``, ``STRING11.5>=0.4``, ``BioGRID2022`` (4.4.214),
  ``CORUM3`` (CORUM 3.0), ``STRINGnew>=0.7``, ``BioGRIDnew`` and
  ``CORUMnew``.

``NAME@SELECT`` and ``NAME@REPORT`` are the two halves. CORUM is split by
complex: the complex names, sorted, are permuted with seed
:data:`SPLIT_SEED` and alternate between the halves, and a REPORT pair that
also lies in a SELECT complex is dropped. Every other reference is split by
pair, on the parity of the md5 of ``"a|b"``.

:param pcs: rows by components.
:param cells_per_guide: ``{gene: cells per guide}``.
:param reference_dir: see :func:`reference_dirs`.
:param settings: the ``ops_eval_*`` settings.
:param arm: the label of the ``arm`` column.
:returns: one row per metric.
spacr.ops_reference.split_references:
The reference names an evaluation split scores.

:param names: base reference names.
:param split: ``'select'``, ``'report'`` or ``'all'``.
:returns: the names with the half appended, or unchanged for ``'all'``.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown split.
spacr.ops_sbs.LibraryMatcher:
The unique closest barcode within a distance, with ``N`` as a wildcard.

One matcher holds the guides and, for a decoy FDR, the decoys, so a read
is matched against both under one uniqueness rule: a read equally close
to a guide and a decoy maps to neither.

:param entries: the barcodes to match against.
Index the barcodes.

:param entries: the barcodes; duplicates are dropped.
spacr.ops_sbs.LibraryMatcher.match:
Match one read.

:param read: the called read; ``N`` is a base that was not measured
    and matches any letter without counting as a mismatch.
:param max_distance: the most mismatches accepted.
:returns: ``(barcode, distance)``, or ``(None, -1)`` when no barcode
    is close enough or two tie for closest.
spacr.ops_sbs.decoy_library:
Base-shuffled decoy barcodes, ``k`` per guide, for a decoy FDR.

Each decoy is a permutation of one guide's letters, so it keeps that
guide's base composition, and it is accepted only when it lies at least
two edits from every guide and every decoy taken before it -- the same
separation the library was designed with. Matched alongside the real
library, a decoy call is a call that cannot be true, and ``k`` decoys per
guide measure a rare false match ``k`` times as precisely.

:param library: the guide barcodes; duplicates are dropped and the rest
    sorted, so the decoys do not depend on the order they were listed in.
:param k: decoys per guide.
:param seed: the shuffle's seed. 1 is the seed of the decode-yield study
    (item 873), whose decoy FDRs this reproduces.
:returns: the decoys, guide by guide and round by round. A guide whose 200
    shuffles all collide gets none in that round.
spacr.ops_sbs.library_calibrated_bases:
Call bases with per-cycle axes learnt from the reads the library names.

The reads are first normalised per cycle and unmixed with brieflow's
median transform. Then, for each read and cycle, the read is matched on
its OTHER cycles; when exactly one guide fits, that guide names the true
base at the masked cycle without looking at it. Per cycle, the median
intensity of the reads labelled with each base is that base's axis; the
four axes, scaled to sum to one, are inverted and every read of the cycle
is unmixed with them. Labels come from the real library only, so a decoy
library matched later stays an independent false-match control. This is
the "S1b" calibration of the decode-yield study (item 873).

:param values: ``(N, cycles, channels)`` from :func:`extract_bases`.
:param library: the guide barcodes.
:param bases: the letter for each channel, in channel order.
:param passes: how often the labels are re-derived from the last calls.
:param min_labels: the fewest labelled reads per base a cycle needs; a
    cycle short of it keeps the median transform.
:param masked: the library's masked index from :func:`_library_index`,
    when the caller keeps one; None builds it.
:returns: ``(data, barcodes, margin)`` as :func:`called_bases` returns
    them.
spacr.ops_sbs.nearest_boundaries:
The two nearest object boundaries of each point, and their objects.

Each object's boundary is its equivalent disc. The ``neighbours`` nearest
centroids are ranked by the gap from the point to their boundary, so the
rule that gives a read to the nearest boundary can also see how close the
runner-up came, which is what the territory rule and a tie test read.

:param points: ``(N, 2)`` positions ``(y, x)``.
:param centroids: ``(M, 2)`` object centroids in the same frame.
:param areas: ``(M,)`` object areas in pixels.
:param neighbours: how many nearest centroids are ranked.
:returns: ``(gap, index)`` -- ``(N, 2)`` float64 gaps, ``inf`` where
    there is no second object, and ``(N, 2)`` indices into
    ``centroids``, -1 where there is none.
spacr.ops_sbs.runner_up_consistent:
Whether a one-mismatch read may count for its guide.

Every mismatched cycle must be one whose call was uncertain -- its margin
below ``max_margin`` -- and whose RUNNER-UP channel is the guide's base,
so the guide is what the read would have said had that cycle tipped the
other way. An ``N`` is not a mismatch.

:param data_row: ``(cycles, channels)``, the intensities the read was
    called from.
:param margin_row: ``(cycles,)``, the per-cycle margins.
:param read: the called read.
:param guide: the guide it matched.
:param max_margin: the largest margin a mismatched cycle may carry.
:param bases: the letter for each channel, in channel order.
:returns: True when every mismatch passes.
spacr.ops_sbs.vote_mapped_reads:
Each object's guide from its reads, matched to the library first.

Every read is matched (:class:`LibraryMatcher`); a read at distance one
or more counts only when ``runner_up_margin`` is given and
:func:`runner_up_consistent` passes. The matched reads vote, each with
weight one, or with ``min(1, quality) + weight_floor`` when
``quality_weighted``. An object takes the top guide when it holds at
least ``min_fraction`` of the votes with no tie, and, when one read is
all that supports it, that read's quality reaches
``single_read_quality``.

:param objects: one object id per read.
:param barcodes: one called barcode per read.
:param quality: one quality per read, the worst cycle's margin.
:param data: ``(N, cycles, channels)``, the intensities called from.
:param margin: ``(N, cycles)``, the per-cycle margins.
:param matcher: the guides, and any decoys, to match against.
:param max_distance: the most mismatches a read may carry.
:param runner_up_margin: the runner-up rule's margin, or None to count
    every match within ``max_distance``.
:param quality_weighted: weight votes by read quality.
:param weight_floor: added to every quality weight.
:param min_fraction: the share of the votes the guide must hold.
:param single_read_quality: the quality a one-read guide needs.
:param impute_missing: let an ``N`` -- a cycle that was not measured --
    match any base; False leaves such reads unmatched.
:param strength: one spot strength per read, for the evidence; None
    records none.
:param evidence: a dict filled with the per-object, per-guide tallies
    behind every vote -- ``votes``, ``exact``, ``corrected``, ``best``,
    ``qualities``, ``strength`` and ``matched`` -- for objects assigned
    or not; None keeps none.
:param bases: the letter for each channel, in channel order.
:returns: ``{object: {"guide", "fraction", "n_support", "n_exact",
    "n_corrected", "n_matched", "n_guides", "vote_top", "vote_total",
    "runner_margin", "quality", "barcode"}}``; ``barcode`` is the
    commonest raw read behind the guide, ``runner_margin`` the top vote
    minus the second over the total.
spacr.ops_sbs.vote_pixels:
Each object's guide from its bright pixels, for objects no read named.

Pixels are called like reads but are not independent -- the pixels of one
spot repeat its call -- so the rule counts pixels, not reads: an object
takes the top exact guide when at least ``min_pixels`` pixels of quality
``min_quality`` or better name it, it holds ``min_fraction`` of them, and
no other guide ties it. This is the "N3" pixel fallback of the
decode-yield study (item 873).

:param objects: one object id per pixel.
:param barcodes: one called barcode per pixel.
:param quality: one quality per pixel.
:param matcher: the guides, and any decoys, to match against exactly.
:param min_quality: the weakest pixel that votes.
:param min_pixels: the fewest agreeing pixels.
:param min_fraction: the share of the matched pixels the guide must hold.
:returns: ``{object: {"guide", "n_pixels", "n_matched", "fraction",
    "runner_margin", "barcode"}}``.
spacr.ops_tvn.nt_pseudo_genes:
Pool non-targeting guides into pseudo-genes of ``size`` guides.

The sorted control guides are permuted with ``default_rng(seed)`` and
taken ``size`` at a time as ``NTpseudo_00``, ``NTpseudo_01``, ...; a
control row whose guide is not listed becomes ``nontargeting_drop``.

:param guides: the guide of every row.
:param genes: the gene of every row.
:param control_guides: every control guide of the screen.
:param size: guides per pseudo-gene.
:param seed: the permutation seed.
:param control_prefix: the control gene prefix.
:returns: the gene names with control rows renamed.
spacr.ops_tvn.profile_cell_tables:
Gene profiles from stored per-well cell tables, without any image step.

The cells of every well are filtered and imputed (:func:`_profile_well`),
embedded by a PCA keeping 99 % of the variance
(:func:`_profile_embedding`), normalised by TVN on the control cells
with the well as batch (:func:`tvn_on_controls`, whitening epsilon
``ops_tvn_whiten_epsilon``; 0 is Brieflow's TVN and is computed at
single precision as Brieflow does, a positive value at double), and
reduced to guides (median of cells) and genes (median of guides, or of
cells), keeping rows with more than ``ops_profile_min_cells`` cells. A
hits table can then keep only active genes and the control rows.

:param settings: read for ``ops_profile_cells`` (a folder of
    ``raw_<well>.parquet`` tables with ``well``, ``sgRNA``, ``gene``,
    ``mitotic`` and feature columns, or ``{plate: folder}``),
    ``ops_profile_wells``, ``plate``, ``ops_profile_recipe``
    (:func:`profile_recipe`), ``ops_tvn_whiten_epsilon``,
    ``ops_profile_min_cells``, ``ops_profile_active_filter``
    (``{"hits_table": path, "fdr": 0.05}``: genes with any ``*_fdr``
    column below ``fdr``), ``ops_profile_shrinkage`` (``'eb_nt'``:
    :func:`spacr.gene_measurement_compare.shrink_gene_profiles`, with
    ``ops_profile_shrinkage_prior_df``), ``ops_profile_weighting``
    (``'contrastive_wiener'``:
    :func:`spacr.gene_measurement_compare.contrastive_weighting`) and
    ``ops_control_prefix``. Shrinkage and weighting run on every gene
    before the active-gene filter, as in the aggregate phase.
:param report: called with progress lines.
:returns: ``(genes, guides, info)``: ``genes`` has ``gene``,
    ``n_cells`` and ``PC_*`` (``w_*`` once weighted); ``guides`` has
    ``guide``, ``gene``, ``n_cells`` and the same columns; ``info``
    counts cells and components, times each step and, when used,
    records the shrinkage or weighting.
:raises ValueError: for a bad setting, a missing table, an unknown
    shrinkage or weighting, or both asked for at once.
spacr.ops_tvn.profile_recipe:
A profile recipe with its defaults filled in and checked.

:param value: any of the :data:`PROFILE_RECIPE` keys. ``lof`` 1 drops
    the 1 % of cells a local outlier factor finds on the mean
    intensities; ``impute`` ``'knn'`` fills gaps by five nearest
    neighbours, as Brieflow does; ``pca`` ``'brieflow'`` fits the PCA on
    100,000 cells standardised by well with Brieflow's sampling; ``agg``
    ``'gene'`` takes the median of all of a gene's cells; ``nt``
    ``'barcode'`` keeps each non-targeting guide as its own row.
:returns: the recipe.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown key or choice.
spacr.ops_tvn.run_profile_phases:
The OPS profile path: stored cell tables -> gene profiles -> metrics.

``profile`` runs :func:`profile_cell_tables` and writes ``genes.parquet``
and ``guides.parquet``; ``evaluate`` embeds the gene rows with more than
``ops_profile_min_cells`` cells (:func:`spacr.ops_reference.embed_gene_profiles`)
and writes ``metrics.csv`` (:func:`spacr.ops_reference.evaluate_gene_profiles`),
``metrics.extra.csv`` (:func:`spacr.ops_reference.specificity_metrics`)
and ``per_gene.csv.gz``. Everything goes to
``<dst_root>/ops_profile/<ops_profile_run>``, with ``runtime.json``
holding the settings, counts and seconds per step.

:param settings: the OPS settings; missing keys take the defaults of
    :func:`spacr.ops_settings.ops_defaults`. Read here: ``dst_root``,
    ``ops_profile_run`` (the plates when empty), ``ops_profile_similarity``
    (empty, ``'cosine'`` or ``'gene_cosine'``), ``ops_profile_min_cells``, ``ops_reference_dir``,
    ``ops_eval_covariates`` (a table with ``gene`` and
    ``cells_per_guide``; the guide table's own cells per guide when
    empty), ``ops_deterministic_blas`` (True holds the BLAS and OpenMP
    pools to one thread, so a re-run of the same settings file gives
    bit-identical tables), the ``ops_eval_*`` settings and those of
    :func:`profile_cell_tables`.
:param phases: ``"profile"``, ``"evaluate"`` or both.
:param report: called with progress lines.
:returns: ``{"folder", "outputs", "info"}``.
:raises ValueError: for a missing ``dst_root``, an unknown similarity,
    or an ``evaluate`` with no profile table to read.

:func:`score_figure_folder` for ``rel_reference``) and their agreement,

spacr.plaque_papers.compare_reported:
Score measured plaque effects against the effects the papers report.

For every reported panel of a figure (``plaque_area``, ``plaque_number``
or ``relative_plaque_size``), each labelling of the wells gives the
measured value of a condition as the mean over its matching wells
(:func:`condition_matches`); the measured effect is that over the
reference condition's, and the reported effect is the panel's value over
its reference value. The summary has, per labelling and readout (area,
number, all), Spearman's rho of the log2 effects (clipped at 0.02), how
many effects that differ from 1 by more than 15% point the same way,
how many agree within 1.5-fold, and a permutation control: rho with the
measured effects shuffled ``compare_permutations`` times (seed
``compare_seed``), its mean, its 95th percentile and a one-sided p.

:param figures: ``{figure: {'quantification': [...], 'regions': {...},
    'labelers': {name: fn(box) -> (strain, treatment) or None}}}``;
    ``quantification`` is the reported panels (``panel``, ``metric``,
    ``values`` with ``strain``, ``treatment``, ``value`` and
    ``is_reference``) and ``regions`` :func:`figure_mode_regions`.
:param settings: ``figure_metric`` (the area readout:
    ``'area'`` or ``'cleared_fraction'``), ``compare_permutations`` and
    ``compare_seed``.
:returns: dict with ``rows`` (a DataFrame: figure, panel, metric,
    labels, strain, treatment, reported_ratio, measured_ratio) and
    ``summary`` (a list of dicts).
spacr.plaque_papers.compare_reported.val: The mean measured value of the wells of one reported condition.
spacr.plaque_papers.condition_matches:
Whether a read figure condition is the reported condition.

spacr.plaque_papers.figure_size_agreemen:
